title: Starter implementation: ship-it blueprint and friction log
content:
Purpose
----
Working blueprint for a single-file 'starter implementation' quickstart we can ship with minimal infra that demonstrates: SDK install, client boot, streaming chat, and a local failover mode. This doc intentionally mixes a polished checklist and scratchpad notes (friction log) so engineers running the experiment can update in-flight. Goal: produce a 10–15 minute demo path + reproducible template that non-Redwood engineers can use to prototype a Redwood-powered feature.

Audience
----
- New integrators (engineers at startups and internal product teams)
- Solutions engineers demoing client impls
- Docs authors and bootcamp facilitators

Constraints and guiding principles
----
- Keep surface area tiny: one markdown repo + one small server script + minimal env vars.
- Multi-language snippets (JS + Python) but canonical repo is Node so we can run the live playground.
- Observability wired to existing telemetry contract (see telemetry matrix below).
- Feature-flagged by default — disable streaming for CI runs.
- Local dev-first: able to run offline with a local stub that emulates Redwood responses.

Ship scope (MVP)
----
1) Quickstart README with 3 commands: install, run, demo.
2) Minimal Node sample that: sets API key from env, calls Redwood /chat, streams tokens to stdout, shows structured tool call.
3) Python snippet in README for parity.
4) Local stub server (single file) that returns deterministic streaming for demo prompts.
5) Telemetry contract: emits request_id, latency_ms, token_count to console and a stubbed metrics endpoint.
6) CI smoke test that runs quickstart and asserts exit codes and a small snapshot.

Minimal file layout (repo)
----
- README.md (quickstart + troubleshooting)
- samples/node/starter.js (executable)
- samples/python/starter.py (snippet parity)
- tools/local_stub.js (very small express server)
- .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml

Quickstart steps (developer facing)
----
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-impl && cd starter-impl
2) npm install (or python -m pip install -r requirements.txt)
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-... OR use local stub: npm run stub &
4) node samples/node/starter.js --prompt "Summarize: why Redwood for inference?"
Expected: streaming tokens printed to console, final JSON with request_id and metrics.

Node starter (concept)
----
// samples/node/starter.js (simplified)
const {Readable} = require('stream');
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
// fallback to stub
const BASE = process.env.REDWOOD_BASE || 'http://localhost:8080';
(async function(){
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/v1/chat`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type':'application/json'},
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'openredwood-lite', messages:[{role:'user',content:process.argv[2]||'hello'}], stream: true})
  });
  // stream parsing + token print
  res.body.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
})();

Telemetry contract (short)
----
Emit a single JSON line after each completion to stdout or metrics sink with fields: request_id, model, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error_code (optional). Example: {\"request_id\":\"req_123\",\"model\":\"openredwood-lite\",\"latency_ms\":72,\"tokens_out\":48}

CI smoke test (sketch)
----
- Start local stub in background
- Run node starter with known prompt
- Capture stdout, assert that: streaming appears, final JSON line exists, exit code 0
- Run Python snippet to check parity

Frictions observed (live notelets)
----
- Users try to pass API key in multiple env var names: REDWOOD_KEY, REDWOOD_API_KEY, RW_API. Decide canonical env var and support deprecated aliases with warning.
- Streaming chunking semantics differ by language runtime (node vs python). Need tiny helper to normalize (we will ship a read_stream helper).
- Local stub needs to mimic SSE and chunk delays else frontends look different. Implement a --delay flag.
- Windows users sometimes fail on export vs setx; add cross-env npm helper or explicit Windows instructions.

Open questions / decisions
----
- Should quickstart include a tiny HTML page demonstrating streaming render? (pros: immediate visual; cons: increases scope) — leaning "optional 2.0"
- Which model should be the canonical example? openredwood-lite vs openredwood-standard. Recommendation: lite for fast demo, standard for examples that exercise longer contexts.
- Do we provide official stub docker image? (ops cost small but helps uniformity).

Rollout plan for release
----
- Internal alpha: share repo with Solutions Eng and two partners (1 week)
- Iterate on friction log and the README (2 weeks)
- Public beta: publish to GitHub org, add npm/package metadata (3rd week)
- Docs: convert README into a short doc page and add to quickstart list (Docs sprint)

Telemetry matrix (fields + thresholds)
----
- request_id: always present
- latency_ms: record median p50/p95 in run (for demo we log single number)
- tokens_out: recorded; warn if > 1024 in quickstart (performance hazard)
- errors: count and surface non-2xx codes

Acceptance criteria
----
- README reproduces demo on fresh machine in <= 12 minutes (including install)
- CI smoke runs in < 3 minutes and passes on main branch on pushes
- No more than 3 "blocking" frictions reported by initial alpha cohort

Housekeeping and next steps (action items)
----
- [ ] Aisha: create skeleton repo + README and push branch starter-impl (due: 2025-11-10)
- [ ] Tom: implement local_stub.js with --delay and SSE parity (due: 2025-11-14)
- [ ] Rina: write Python parity starter snippet and CI job (due: 2025-11-17)
- [ ] Evan: draft docs page and link to telemetry contract (due: 2025-11-20)
- [ ] Team: schedule 30-min playtest with Solutions Eng (target: week of 2025-11-24)

Notes for whoever picks this up later:
- Keep the sample code intentionally minimal; we want clear patterns, not full SDK features.
- If upstream SDK changes interface, update README with the exact pinned commit used for the demo.
- Capture one short screencast (30–60s) of the streaming behavior for the README.

Appendix: quick Windows tip (copy-paste for README)
----
Use PowerShell to set env var for the session: $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"sk-test-...\"
Start stub: node tools/local_stub.js &
Run sample: node samples/node/starter.js \"hello world\"

Change log (live)
----

2025-11-20 - added telemetry contract notes + CI sketch (Rina)
2026-03-10 - updated last_modified with Windows tips and rollout timeline (Aisha)

Friction log (short journal)
----
- 2025-11-12: user reported confusing error when REDWOOD_API_KEY missing; added clearer error message and link to create key page.
- 2025-11-15: stub SSE timing caused UI flicker; added --delay param and default 50ms chunk spacing.
- 2025-12-01: telemetry log format variant observed; normalize to single JSON line at completion for ease of grep.

End of doc.
